source_notes: Project 1 of the AI Builder Journey focused on building a RAG Knowledge Assistant for answering questions using approved documents. I worked with the RAG flow of documents, chunks, embeddings, vector store, retrieval, LLM, and answer generation.
audience: Builders and clients interested in AI and Python projects
key_lesson: RAG connects retrieval with generation so an AI application can use relevant information from provided documents when answering questions.
call_to_action: Learn the basic RAG workflow and understand how retrieval supports an AI answer.

source_notes: While working on Project 1, I focused on making answers more trustworthy by using retrieved context and checking whether the answer was supported by the provided documents.
audience: AI builders learning RAG and practical AI applications
key_lesson: A RAG system should use retrieved information as context and should avoid presenting unsupported information as if it came from the supplied documents.
call_to_action: Try a small RAG project and test both answerable and unanswerable questions.

source_notes: Project 2 focused on designing an AI-assisted lead qualification system in Python. I worked with lead input, classification, structured output, recommended next actions, and reply drafting.
audience: Builders and clients interested in AI, freelancing, and Python projects
key_lesson: An AI application becomes more useful when model output is connected to structured data and clear application logic.
call_to_action: Explore how structured AI output can be used inside a Python application.

source_notes: During Project 2, I worked on generating personalized reply drafts and added rules to avoid unsupported promises or invented information. Human approval remained part of the process.
audience: AI builders interested in responsible AI applications
key_lesson: AI-generated communication should be treated as a draft that can be reviewed rather than blindly accepted.
call_to_action: Think about where human review should remain in an AI workflow.

source_notes: In Project 2, I added follow-up tracking and a dashboard to organize lead information, follow-up dates, priorities, categories, and leads requiring attention.
audience: Builders interested in practical Python and AI systems
key_lesson: Combining AI results with Python logic, stored data, and a dashboard can turn separate AI features into a more organized application workflow.
call_to_action: Identify one repetitive workflow that could be improved by combining AI with Python logic.
